idea: When to replace old plumbing pipes
title: Is It Time to Repipe Your Home? Key Signs to Watch For
description: Pipes don't last forever, and waiting for a major burst can lead to costly water damage. Galvanized steel pipes, common in older homes, typically degrade from the inside out after 40 to 50 years. As rust and mineral buildup choke off water flow, you may notice low water pressure, discolored tap water, or frequent pinhole leaks. Lead and unlined iron pipes also pose health and reliability risks. If your home still relies on original metallic supply lines, have a licensed plumber inspect their condition to evaluate pipe wall thickness and plan a modern replacement before an emergency happens.
image_prompt: A professional high-detail vertical photograph taken inside a well-lit residential basement utility space. In the central foreground, a plumber wearing blue nitrile gloves holds a sliced cross-section of an old 3/4-inch galvanized steel water pipe. The open end of the pipe clearly reveals heavy internal rust accumulation, tuberculation, and thick mineral scale narrowing the inner opening to a small pinhole. In the soft-focus background, properly mounted clean copper and PEX water lines run along neat wooden ceiling joists. Sharp focus on the corroded pipe cross-section, showing realistic rough metallic texture, flaking iron oxide, and authentic pipe wall thickness. Natural directional studio lighting, realistic depth of field, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio, shot on 85mm lens, photorealistic commercial photography.
